items.objective: 5.2 Design effective escalation and ambiguity resolution patterns
items.stem: A customer writes to the resolution agent: "The coffee grinder I bought in March has stopped working. I want a new one." Two remedies in the policy fit that sentence. The 30-day return window has closed, but the item carries a 24-month manufacturer warranty that would ship a replacement in about ten days, and the customer also holds enough store credit to buy a replacement outright today. The two paths differ in cost to the customer, in delivery time, and in whether the original unit must be returned. The agent currently picks one without comment and proceeds. What should the design require?

options.text: Instruct the agent to ask one disambiguating question that names both remedies and the consequence that separates them, then act on the answer, since the customer's request is ambiguous rather than unsupported.
Instruct the agent to default to the warranty replacement whenever both paths are open, since it is the remedy the manufacturer funds and the customer keeps their store credit for a later purchase.
Escalate every request that matches more than one remedy to a human, on the basis that choosing between two chargeable outcomes is a commercial decision an autonomous agent should not take.
Score how well the request matches each remedy against the policy text and proceed with the higher-scoring remedy, escalating only when the two scores sit within a configured margin of each other.

items.explanation: The request is ambiguous, not uncovered: the policy authorises both outcomes and only the customer knows which trade-off they want. The documented pattern for ambiguity is to resolve it with the customer through a clarifying question rather than to select on a heuristic, which is the same discipline applied to multiple tool matches. One question that names both remedies and the consequence separating them settles the case inside the conversation and keeps first-contact resolution intact.

rationales.B: A house default is heuristic selection under a business-sounding justification; it silently decides a trade-off between waiting ten days and paying today that belongs to the customer, and it is the behaviour the review is objecting to.
rationales.C: None of the escalation triggers applies: the customer has not asked for a human, the policy covers both remedies rather than being silent, and the agent can make progress with a single question, so escalating discards a case it is equipped to resolve.
rationales.D: Both remedies genuinely match the request, so the score is measuring the wrong quantity: what separates them is whether the customer would rather wait ten days at no cost or spend store credit today, and no match against the policy text can observe that preference.

items.objective: 5.3 Implement error propagation strategies across multi-agent systems
items.stem: A web-search subagent runs eight queries for a coordinator. Two return no matches because the corpus genuinely contains nothing on those terms; one returns HTTP 504 from the upstream provider after 30 seconds. The subagent currently reports all three the same way, as {"results": []}. The coordinator's report states that no evidence exists for all three topics. What should the subagent return instead?

options.text: Have the subagent convert any query that ends in a transport error into an empty result once its retries are spent, so the coordinator receives one uniform result shape for all eight queries and never has to branch on failure handling.
Report the batch as a single aggregate coverage percentage with no per-query status, so the coordinator can see at a glance how much of the search plan completed and weight the findings accordingly.
Report the two completed queries that matched nothing as valid empty results, and report the timed-out query as an access failure carrying the attempted query and any partial results.

Have the subagent record the timed-out query as an empty result but send the timeout to the application's telemetry rather than to the coordinator, so operators can see the outage without a search problem changing what the report says.

items.explanation: The distinction that matters is between a valid empty result, which is a real answer to a question that was actually asked, and an access failure, where the question was never answered at all. Only the coordinator can decide what to do about the second, so it has to be able to tell them apart, and attaching the attempted query and any partial results is what lets it retry, reroute to another source, or annotate a coverage gap rather than concluding that no evidence exists.

rationales.A: Absorbing an unanswered query into the empty-result shape is exactly the conflation that produced the false finding; a uniform shape is convenient for the caller and removes the one signal the caller needs.
rationales.B: A completion percentage says how much finished but not which topics are unsupported or why, so the coordinator still cannot tell an answered question from an unanswered one and cannot act on the difference.
rationales.D: Telemetry serves the operator, not the reasoning agent: the coordinator still sees an empty result, still reports that no evidence exists, and the record of why is in a system that has no part in building the report.

items.objective: 5.2 Design effective escalation and ambiguity resolution patterns
items.stem: A customer writes to the resolution agent: "Third late delivery this month and I am completely fed up with this." They do not ask for a person. lookup_order shows the parcel four days past its promised date and held at a carrier depot, and the policy plainly authorises a free reship plus a refund of the delivery fee, both of which the agent is able to execute itself. The agent currently reads the tone as an escalation signal and calls escalate_to_human without replying. What should the design require instead?

options.text: Acknowledge the frustration, then offer the free reship and the delivery-fee refund that the agent can carry out now, and escalate only if the customer answers by asking for a person or by restating that preference.

Escalate on any message carrying strong negative language, since a customer who has already had three failures this month will be angrier still if an automated agent attempts a remedy and gets it wrong, and a human can offer the same reship and the same fee refund in any case.

Process the reship and the delivery-fee refund straight away and reply with the new tracking number alone, since the customer wants the parcel rather than an apology and naming the complaint invites further discussion.
Apologise, tell the customer that a specialist will review the delivery history, and leave the case in the queue so that no remedy is chosen before the account has been looked at.

items.explanation: The escalation triggers are an explicit request for a human, a policy gap, and an inability to make meaningful progress. Strong feeling on its own is none of them. Where the issue sits inside what the agent is authorised and able to do, the pattern is to acknowledge how the customer feels and to offer the remedy in the same reply, escalating only if the customer then asks for a person or repeats that preference. Escalating on tone alone gives away a case that could have closed on first contact.

rationales.B: None of the escalation triggers is present, and the remedy is not a judgement call: the policy authorises both parts of it and the agent can execute both. Handing the case off costs the customer a fourth wait for something that could be settled in this reply.
rationales.C: Executing the remedy silently answers the delivery problem and ignores the complaint the customer actually made. Acknowledging the frustration is what separates a resolution the customer accepts from one that produces a second contact an hour later.
rationales.D: This neither acknowledges nor resolves: it defers a case the policy already covers, and a promise to review later is a worse outcome than the immediate escalation being corrected.

items.objective: 5.3 Implement error propagation strategies across multi-agent systems
items.stem: A research coordinator delegates a market study to five subagents. The document-analysis subagent fails when the internal knowledge-base gateway is unavailable for about four minutes. The coordinator currently aborts the whole run and returns nothing, discarding the work of the four subagents that finished successfully. Which TWO changes bring the design in line with the documented error-propagation pattern? (Select TWO)

options.text: Have the coordinator absorb the failure and synthesize from the four successful result sets, recording the coverage of the run in the job log so that one flaky dependency never blocks delivery of the finished study.

Set maxBudgetUsd on the run so a subagent stuck against a failing dependency cannot burn spend, and let the resulting error_max_budget_usd subtype end the query with whatever partial results it holds.
Lower CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS to four so the document-analysis subagent runs after the others and its failure arrives once the rest of the work is already banked.

Have the document-analysis subagent retry the gateway itself across the outage window and, if it still cannot read the corpus, hand back the queries it ran, the documents it did reach, and the reason it stopped.
Build the study from the four result sets that did arrive and mark, in the report itself, which conclusions rest on evidence and which subject areas nothing could be read for.
Have the coordinator immediately re-spawn the failed subagent against the next model in the fallback chain and hold the synthesis step until that retry returns a result.

items.explanation: The prescribed shape has two halves. A failure that clears on its own is handled where it happened, inside the subagent, and only what that subagent cannot settle travels upward carrying the attempt and whatever it did obtain. The coordinator then finishes the job with the material it has and says in the report which conclusions rest on evidence and which subject areas nothing was read for, so a reader can tell a supported finding from a hole.

rationales.A: Presenting a study built on four of five sources as finished is the silent-suppression anti-pattern; a note in the job log is invisible to the person reading the study, who has no way to know that a whole subject area rests on nothing.
rationales.B: A spend cap limits cost, not error handling. It ends the entire query on a budget subtype, which is the same all-or-nothing termination the design is trying to escape, and a gateway outage costs almost nothing to hit.
rationales.C: The concurrency cap governs how many subagents run at once, not ordering or failure semantics, and it does nothing about a gateway outage or about what the coordinator does with the failure.
rationales.F: A model fallback chain addresses API errors from the model, not an unreachable knowledge-base gateway, and blocking synthesis on the retry reintroduces the dependency of the whole run on one subagent.

items.objective: 5.3 Implement error propagation strategies across multi-agent systems
items.stem: A nightly Agent SDK job regenerates module documentation for a large repository. The wrapper ends with: if result.subtype == "success": publish(result.result) else: log("run failed"). About one night in six nothing is published, the log line is the only record, and the finance dashboard still shows spend for those nights. The on-call engineer cannot tell whether the run ran out of turns, hit a budget ceiling, or crashed. Which change gives the operator what is needed?

options.text: Wrap the query in a try/except and retry the whole run once on any exception, since the result message reports only success or failure and carries no further detail about why a run ended.
Branch on stop_reason instead of subtype, since stop_reason distinguishes turn exhaustion, budget exhaustion and execution errors while subtype only reports whether the run succeeded.

Branch on the specific subtype (error_max_turns, error_max_budget_usd, error_during_execution, error_max_structured_output_retries) and log total_cost_usd, num_turns and session_id, which every result carries.

Treat the absence of a result field as the failure signal and publish the text of the last assistant message received instead, on the basis that partially regenerated module documentation is more useful to the team the next morning than nothing at all.

items.explanation: The result message subtype is the primary termination signal and already names the failure precisely. Every subtype, including the failures, still carries total_cost_usd, usage, num_turns and session_id, so a failed run can be costed and resumed. Branching on the specific subtype and logging those fields turns an opaque "run failed" into an actionable record.

rationales.A: The premise is wrong: the result already distinguishes several failure modes, and blind retries would repeat a run that exhausted turns or budget with the same settings and the same outcome.
rationales.B: This inverts the two fields. The subtype carries the termination taxonomy; stop_reason reports why the model's final turn ended, and it is null on a result synthesized after a crash.
rationales.D: The result text is present only on a successful subtype, and publishing whatever the last assistant message happened to contain would ship partial documentation as if it were complete.

items.objective: 5.3 Implement error propagation strategies across multi-agent systems
items.stem: A Claude Code coordinator built on the Agent SDK delegates each module of a large refactor to a subagent through the Agent tool and merges what comes back. When the shared type-index service answers 503, the affected subagent's own transcript shows it diagnosed the outage precisely: the endpoint that failed, the three files it had already rewritten, and a Grep fallback over src/ that it judged workable. The coordinator receives only "could not complete the payments module" and has nothing to act on. Which change gives the coordinator the diagnosis?

options.text: Make the subagent's final message a structured failure report naming the failure type, the call that failed, the files already rewritten and the fallback it can offer, because intermediate tool calls and results stay inside the subagent and only that final message returns to the parent as the Agent tool result.

Have the coordinator locate the subagent's transcript under ~/.claude/projects/ and parse its tool_result blocks for the diagnosis, since subagent transcripts are written to separate files and persist independently of the main conversation.

Spawn the module subagents as forks of the coordinator's conversation, so that parent and child share one context and the coordinator can read the subagent's intermediate tool results directly instead of waiting for a summary.
Let the 503 propagate out of the subagent uncaught so the Agent tool result comes back marked as an error, and branch the coordinator on that flag rather than on the text of the final message.

items.explanation: Delegation isolates context in both directions. A subagent's intermediate tool calls and results stay inside it, and the parent receives its final message as the Agent tool result and nothing else. Anything the coordinator needs in order to retry, reroute or annotate therefore has to be composed into that final message, which makes the subagent's return contract the place to put the failure type, what was attempted, what was already finished and the alternative on offer.

rationales.B: The transcript is a debugging artefact on the machine that ran the subagent, not a return channel. The coordinator would have to know the subagent's session id, parse an internal file format, and get there before the cleanup period removes it, all to recover text the subagent could have written into its own result.
rationales.C: A fork copies the parent's conversation into the child when it is spawned; it does not send the child's turns back. Intermediate tool calls and results stay inside the subagent either way, so the coordinator would still see only the final message.
rationales.D: An error flag says that something failed, not what failed or what to do instead, so the coordinator ends up where it is today. The endpoint, the three rewritten files and the workable fallback still have to be in the message before anything can act on them.

items.objective: 5.4 Manage context effectively in large codebase exploration
items.stem: A team is using Claude Code to trace the settlement path through a 12,000-file payments monorepo before refactoring it. In the first hour Claude names concrete artefacts it has read: SettlementLedgerRepo, the retry wrapper in billing/settle/retry.go, and the two queues that feed them. Two hours later, asked which repository writes the reversal record, Claude answers in terms of 'a typical ledger repository pattern' and no longer names the classes it found earlier. Which change BEST counteracts this?

options.text: Move the auto-compact point with `/autocompact 500k` so that the accumulated exploration history survives further into the session before the automatic pass rewrites the whole conversation into a summary of the work so far.
Have Claude append each confirmed finding to a scratchpad file such as `docs/settlement-notes.md`, and point later prompts at that file so the specific names outlive the context boundary.
Move the exploration into the built-in `Explore` subagent and resume that subagent whenever an earlier finding needs to be recalled in detail.

Add the discovered class names to `.claude/rules/settlement.md` with `paths:` frontmatter matching `billing/**`, so that the accumulated detail is reloaded automatically whenever Claude next opens a settlement source file.

items.explanation: The symptom is context degradation in an extended session: the model drifts from specific discovered artefacts to generic pattern language once the concrete findings have been summarized away. The documented counter is a scratchpad file. Findings are written to disk as they are confirmed and re-read on demand, so the specifics live outside the conversation history that compaction rewrites, and the same file also seeds the next exploration phase.

rationales.A: Moving where the automatic pass runs only changes when the history is rewritten. It cannot exceed the model's context window, the verbose discovery output keeps accumulating either way, and recall of specifics degrades as the window fills, before any compaction runs. Nothing is written to disk, so there is no place to recover the class names from.
rationales.C: `Explore` is read-only and one-shot: it returns no agentId and therefore cannot be resumed. It also deliberately skips CLAUDE.md and git status to keep costs low, so it is the wrong vehicle for a long, resumable investigation.
rationales.D: `.claude/rules/` carries project conventions, not runtime discoveries, and a rule with `paths:` frontmatter is not re-injected after compaction until Claude next reads a matching file, so the details would be missing exactly when they are needed.

items.objective: 5.4 Manage context effectively in large codebase exploration
items.stem: A developer-productivity agent built on the Agent SDK has spent twenty turns helping an engineer map an unfamiliar billing service: which packages are in scope, which three modules carry the settlement logic, and which generated directories to ignore. It then delegates with an Agent tool call whose prompt reads: 'Continue the analysis of the modules we identified and skip the directories we agreed to ignore.' The code-analysis subagent returns a generic description of how billing services are usually layered and names none of the modules. The coordinator's `allowedTools` includes `Agent`, and no error or limit message appears. What is the root cause?

options.text: The subagent hit its `maxTurns` limit, so the Agent tool result was marked partial and the coordinator read a truncated analysis instead of the finished one.

The subagent inherited the coordinator's conversation, but its `settingSources` configuration omitted `project`, so the project CLAUDE.md holding the module layout and the ignore list was never loaded into its session at all, leaving it to reason from the repository name alone.
`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` is at its default, so the analysis subagent could not delegate its own file reads and fell back to a single shallow pass over the service.

A non-fork subagent starts with a fresh, isolated context window and receives only the Agent tool's prompt string, so the module names, the ignore list and the twenty turns of prior findings had to be written into that prompt explicitly.

items.explanation: Delegation does not share context. A non-fork subagent starts with a fresh, isolated context window: it does not see the parent's conversation history, tool results, system prompt, auto memory or the files the parent has already read. The only content that crosses is the Agent tool's prompt string, plus the subagent's own AgentDefinition prompt, project CLAUDE.md via settingSources, and its tool definitions. A prompt that says 'the modules we identified' therefore references nothing the subagent can see, which is exactly the generic output observed. Summarizing the exploration phase and injecting that summary into the subagent's initial prompt is the fix.

rationales.A: A subagent stopped at `maxTurns` has its Agent tool result explicitly marked partial so the parent knows the run is unfinished. The stem states no limit message appeared, and truncation would not turn specific module analysis into generic background.
rationales.B: A non-fork subagent does not inherit the parent's conversation at all, so the premise is wrong. Loading project CLAUDE.md would supply standing project conventions, not the twenty turns of scoping and the ignore list agreed in this session.
rationales.C: The default spawn depth is three layers below the main agent, which leaves this first-level subagent free to delegate. At the depth cap Claude Code simply leaves the bottom-layer subagent unable to spawn, so it does the delegated work itself - it does not degrade a specific analysis into generic background. The concurrency cap, by contrast, does surface a visible `Concurrent subagent limit reached` tool result, which the stem rules out.

items.objective: 5.4 Manage context effectively in large codebase exploration
items.stem: Halfway through a multi-file refactor in Claude Code, an engineer sees the context indicator near its limit. Most of the window is taken up by verbose `Grep` and `Read` output from the discovery phase, which is now finished. The engineer wants to keep working on the same refactor, with the decisions already agreed still in force. Which in-session control fits?

options.text: Run `/clear` to begin with an empty context, then restate the refactor goal and the agreed decisions so the session continues with a clean window.
Run `/context` to display the live breakdown of what is consuming the window along with its optimization suggestions for the current session.
Run `/compact` with instructions naming the refactor, replacing the history with a focused summary while the same conversation continues.
Open `/rewind` and choose Restore code and conversation to return the session and the working tree to the checkpoint taken before discovery began.

items.explanation: `/compact [instructions]` replaces the conversation history with a summary that can be focused on what you name, and the conversation carries on. That is the control for staying on task when discovery output has filled the window. Project-root CLAUDE.md, unscoped rules, auto memory and any plan mode plan are re-injected from disk afterwards, so the durable project context is not lost either.

rationales.A: `/clear` starts an empty context and discards the working state. It is the control for switching to unrelated work, not for continuing a task, and it forces the engineer to reconstruct decisions by hand.
rationales.B: `/context` only reports what is consuming the window. It is a useful diagnostic before choosing an action, but on its own it frees nothing and the session remains at its limit.
rationales.D: Restore code and conversation rolls the working tree back to an earlier checkpoint, undoing the refactor edits already made. The goal is to reduce context, not to discard completed work.

items.objective: 5.4 Manage context effectively in large codebase exploration
items.stem: A nightly worker drives the support resolution agent through a queue of 400 billing disputes. Each dispute takes several MCP tool calls, and `process_refund` is not idempotent. Last night the worker container was evicted mid-batch; the replacement worker restarted the batch from the top and re-refunded eleven customers who had already been paid. Which design prevents a repeat?

options.text: Have every worker write a durable record to shared storage the moment a refund is confirmed, and have the coordinator read that record on restart and pass the ids already settled into each agent's prompt before any dispute is picked up again.
Wrap the whole batch in one long-lived session and rely on automatic compaction to carry the list of completed disputes forward inside the summary it produces.
Append each completed dispute id to the project CLAUDE.md, which is loaded from disk at session start and re-injected after every compaction.

Have each agent export its state to a known location once the batch finishes, and set a high `maxTurns` and a generous `maxBudgetUsd` so the worker is far less likely to terminate before that export has been written.

items.explanation: Crash recovery is a state-persistence problem, not a context problem. Progress has to be committed to durable storage as it happens, and the restarted run has to read that record before it does anything, so the disputes already paid are skipped. Because a subagent receives only its prompt, feeding the recovered ids into the prompt is the step that actually makes the recovered state visible to the agent doing the work.

rationales.B: Progressive summarization is exactly what condenses precise values such as dispute ids and refund amounts into vague prose, and the summary lives inside a process that has just been evicted. It is not durable state.
rationales.C: CLAUDE.md reloads at session start and after compaction, not per request, and in either case it is project context rather than a runtime ledger. Writing per-run transaction state into it pollutes every future session, grows without bound, and still offers no guarantee that a dispute was actually paid.
rationales.D: An export written only once the batch finishes is never written when the batch is the thing that fails, and raising limits addresses one termination cause while doing nothing about container eviction, host failure or deployment. Any restart still replays the queue.

items.objective: 5.4 Manage context effectively in large codebase exploration
items.stem: A developer-productivity agent on the Agent SDK answers onboarding questions from new hires about an unfamiliar 40-service telemetry platform. Answering one question typically takes forty `Grep` and `Read` calls, and every raw match and file body stays in the coordinator's transcript afterwards. By the fourth question the window is nearly full and the coordinator has begun losing the architectural picture it assembled from the first three answers. Which change BEST preserves that high-level understanding across a long queue of questions?

options.text: Run `/compact` with instructions after each question, so the previous answer's discovery output is replaced by a focused summary before the next question begins.

Raise the coordinator's `maxTurns` and move it to a model with a larger context window, so that forty tool calls per question and their full output can accumulate across the whole queue without the window filling up at all.

Delegate each specific question to its own subagent - trace the ingestion dependencies, list every integration test - so the raw matches stay in that subagent's context window and only its summary comes back.

Register a `PostToolUse` hook that rewrites each `Grep` and `Read` result down to the matching lines before it is appended to the transcript, so that every tool result costs a small fraction of what it costs now.

items.explanation: Isolating verbose exploration output is what delegation is for. A subagent runs in its own context window, so the forty raw matches and file bodies for a question stay there and only the relevant summary returns to the main conversation. The coordinator's window then holds answers rather than evidence, which is what preserves the architectural picture across a long queue, and independent questions can be investigated by several subagents at once.

rationales.A: Compaction reclaims the space but it rewrites the whole conversation, including the architectural picture built from the earlier answers - the very thing the stem says is being lost. It also runs only after the raw output has already been read into the window and paid for.
rationales.B: A larger window and a higher turn budget defer the ceiling without changing what accumulates. Forty raw tool results per question still sit between the coordinator and its own conclusions, and recall degrades as the window fills, well before any limit is reached.
rationales.D: Trimming each result shrinks the residue but does not isolate it: every question's leftovers still land in the one window the coordinator uses to hold the architecture. It is a useful complement to delegation, not a substitute for it.

items.objective: 5.5 Design human review workflows and confidence calibration
items.stem: An extraction pipeline handles twelve document types (invoices, bills of lading, insurance certificates and nine others) against a JSON schema of 30 fields. On a 5,000-document labelled validation set it scores 97.2% field-level accuracy overall. The operations lead proposes retiring human review entirely and auto-approving every extraction. What must be done before that decision can be defended?

options.text: Break the measured accuracy out by document type and by field and confirm that each segment meets the target, because an aggregate can hide a type or a field far below it.
Route on the field-level confidence scores, whose threshold was calibrated last year against a labelled set of invoices, and auto-approve every extraction that clears that calibrated cut.

Add `minimum` and `maximum` constraints on the confidence property in the `output_config.format` JSON schema, so that any out-of-range score is rejected by the API before an extraction can reach the auto-approval step.
Run every document three times through the same schema and auto-approve only where all three runs agree on every field, treating any disagreement between the runs as a hallucination signal.

items.explanation: A single aggregate accuracy number can mask poor performance on specific document types or specific fields. An overall 97.2% is consistent with one rare document type extracting at 70%, or one field such as tax code failing across the board, both of which would be shipped straight into production. The blueprint requires accuracy validated by document type and field segment before human review is reduced.

rationales.B: The cut is calibrated, but on the wrong population and at the wrong grain. It was measured on invoices alone, and the pipeline now spans twelve document types, so nothing establishes that it transfers. Even on invoices it fixes an overall rate rather than showing that every field meets the target.
rationales.C: Schema constraints govern the shape of the output, not its truth, and numerical constraints such as `minimum` and `maximum` are in any case not supported in structured output schemas - the SDKs strip them from the wire schema. A well-formed score can still be badly wrong.
rationales.D: Best-of-N consistency checking is a real technique for surfacing hallucination, but it measures agreement between runs rather than accuracy per segment, and it triples cost across the whole corpus while leaving the masking problem untouched.

items.objective: 5.5 Design human review workflows and confidence calibration
items.stem: The extraction service routes any document with a low confidence score to a human reviewer and auto-approves the rest. Reviewers therefore only ever see the low-confidence queue, whose measured error rate is stable. A supplier then changed its invoice template, and for six weeks the pipeline extracted the wrong tax code from those invoices with high confidence; the problem surfaced only when a downstream finance reconciliation failed. Which change to the review workflow would have caught this?

options.text: Apply stratified random sampling inside the existing low-confidence review queue, so that every document type and every supplier is represented in what the reviewers work through each week.

Have reviewers score a scheduled random draw from the auto-approved population itself, taken in proportion to supplier and document type, so that the bucket the service stopped checking still yields a measured error rate and unfamiliar failure shapes become visible.
Have the model re-read each auto-approved extraction in a second pass and flag any value it would now change, routing only the flagged extractions to a human reviewer.
Require a supporting direct quote for every extracted field and retract any field whose quote cannot be located verbatim in the source document before approval.

items.explanation: Sampling only the low-confidence bucket measures nothing about the extractions the service has decided to stop checking. A scheduled random draw from the auto-approved population, taken in proportion to the strata that matter, is what produces an ongoing error-rate estimate for that population and what surfaces novel error patterns, such as a changed template, that no confidence signal flagged.

rationales.A: Sampling within the queue the system already doubts makes that queue better covered but measures nothing about the population it stopped checking. The failing invoices carried high confidence and so never entered this queue at all.
rationales.C: Model self-verification uses the same model and the same misreading of the new template, so it is likely to confirm the original extraction. It also produces no measurement of the error rate in the auto-approved population.
rationales.D: Quote-first grounding reduces fabricated content, but a tax code copied confidently from the wrong region of a redesigned template will have a valid verbatim quote behind it, so the retraction rule never fires.

items.objective: 5.5 Design human review workflows and confidence calibration
items.stem: The support resolution agent reads a customer's uploaded receipt and self-reports a confidence score for each value it pulls out, including the refund amount. The team now has to choose the score below which a case is routed to a human reviewer before `process_refund` runs. One engineer proposes 0.7 on the grounds that it looks about right. What is the documented basis for setting that threshold?

options.text: Set it to the mean confidence observed across the last 1,000 resolved cases, so that roughly half of live traffic is routed to a reviewer.

Have the model output, alongside each field score, the review threshold it recommends for that particular receipt, and route on the model's own per-document recommendation so that the cut adapts to how hard each receipt was to read.
Set it from reviewer capacity alone, choosing whichever value fills the available review hours each day without overflowing into the next shift.
Calibrate it against a labelled validation set, measuring the accuracy actually observed at each band of the self-reported score and cutting where that measured accuracy meets the target.

items.explanation: Self-reported field-level confidence is a usable routing signal, but only once it has been calibrated: a labelled validation set tells you what accuracy is actually observed at each band of the score, and the threshold is then placed where measured accuracy meets the target. Without that mapping the number is an uninterpreted model output and any cut chosen from it is arbitrary.

rationales.A: The mean of an uncalibrated score is still uncalibrated. It fixes the split of traffic rather than the accuracy of what is auto-approved, and it moves whenever the mix of incoming documents changes.
rationales.B: A self-recommended threshold is the same self-report problem one level removed. The model has no measurement of its own field-level error rate to derive a threshold from, so it cannot supply a defensible cut, and a per-document cut cannot be audited against any target.
rationales.C: Capacity determines how much review the team can afford, not where the accuracy risk sits. Used alone it would auto-approve genuinely uncertain refunds on a quiet day and send safe ones to review on a busy one.

items.objective: 5.5 Design human review workflows and confidence calibration
items.stem: A platform team gates its Claude Code merge queue on a per-change confidence score. Before launch they calibrated the gate properly: on a labelled set of 2,000 historical changes they measured the observed defect rate in each confidence band and put the auto-merge cut at 0.9, the band where measured defects met their target. Six months on, the auto-merged population carries a materially higher escaped-defect rate than the reviewed population, and the team's work has shifted from CRUD endpoints toward concurrency-sensitive service code. What does the review workflow MOST need now?

options.text: Recalibrate once against the original 2,000-change labelled set, re-deriving the observed defect rate in each confidence band and moving the auto-merge cut to whichever value meets the target on that set.

Raise the auto-merge cut from 0.9 to 0.98 so that only the most confident changes bypass review, restoring margin against the defects now escaping, and leave the bands derived from the original labelled set otherwise untouched.
Continuing measurement of the merged population: sample auto-merged changes on a schedule, measure escaped defects per change type, and move the cut as those measurements move.
Move generation of concurrency-sensitive service code to a larger model, treating the escaped defects as a capability shortfall rather than a gating problem.

items.explanation: Calibration is not a one-off exercise. A cut derived once from a historical labelled set holds only while the population being gated still resembles the population it was measured on, and here the mix of work has moved. What the workflow needs is ongoing error-rate measurement of the auto-merged population itself: a sample of merged changes reviewed on a continuing basis, escaped defects counted per change type, and the cut moved when the measurement moves. That is also the only mechanism that surfaces a failure mode the original bands never contained.

rationales.A: Re-deriving bands from the same historical set measures the old mix of work again, and it is another single point in time. It cannot see the concurrency-sensitive changes now driving the escapes, and six months from now it is stale in exactly the same way.
rationales.B: Moving the cut without measuring anything trades throughput for an unquantified amount of safety. Nothing establishes that 0.98 meets the target on the current mix of work, and the gate stays blind to whatever keeps escaping above it.
rationales.D: Capability and calibration are separate properties. A stronger model may write better concurrency code and still report confidence that does not track its own error rate, so an unmeasured gate remains unjustified.

items.objective: 5.5 Design human review workflows and confidence calibration
items.stem: Quality assurance for the support resolution agent has enough reviewer capacity to inspect about 15% of resolved cases. The architect must decide which cases that capacity is spent on. Which TWO selection criteria should drive the routing? (Select TWO)

options.text: Cases that consumed the most tokens overall, on the basis that a long conversation correlates with a higher chance of a summarization error somewhere in it.
Cases where the agent's calibrated confidence in the customer identity match was high, on the basis that a confident identification means the rest of the case ran on solid data.
Cases resolved in the fewest turns, on the basis that a very fast resolution suggests the agent did not investigate the account history thoroughly.
Cases handled during the busiest hour of the day, when queue depth was highest and the agent was competing for backend tool capacity.
Cases where the calibrated field-level confidence for a value that decided the outcome, such as the refund amount, falls in the low-confidence band.
Cases where the customer's supplied documents are ambiguous or contradict each other, for example a receipt total that disagrees with the stored order record.

items.explanation: With limited reviewer capacity, review is prioritised where the risk of an incorrect outcome is highest: extractions whose calibrated confidence sits in the low band, and cases whose source documents are ambiguous or mutually contradictory so that no single reading is clearly right. Both criteria are properties of the evidence and of a measured signal, which is what makes them defensible ways to spend a fixed review budget.

rationales.A: Token consumption tracks conversation length and tool verbosity, not the correctness of the decision. Routing on it would fill the queue with thorough, correct investigations while missing short cases decided on a bad value.
rationales.B: This is a measured, calibrated signal, but about the wrong quantity and pointing the wrong way. Confidence in the identity match says nothing about the refund amount read off the receipt, which is the value that decides the outcome, and high confidence is a reason to spend scarce review capacity elsewhere.
rationales.C: Turn count measures how quickly the agent reached an answer, not whether the answer was right. Many straightforward cases legitimately resolve in very few turns.
rationales.D: Time of day and queue depth are operational load metrics. They say nothing about the evidence quality or the confidence of any particular extraction, so they would spread review effort at random.

items.objective: 5.6 Preserve information provenance and handle uncertainty in multi-source synthesis
items.stem: A synthesis subagent in the research system produces the efficacy section of a report on a drug candidate. Three of its statements come from a replicated multi-site trial, one from a single unblinded pilot of nine patients whose own authors described the result as preliminary, and one from the manufacturer's press release. All five arrive in the report as flat declarative sentences in one list, and a reviewer acted on the pilot figure as though it were settled. Which change to the synthesis contract fixes this?

options.text: Attach a source identifier and a verbatim supporting excerpt to every statement in the section, so that a reader who doubts one of the five figures can follow it back to the document it was taken from without re-reading the corpus.

Have the synthesis subagent rank the five sources by publisher authority and report only the statements drawn from the two highest-ranked ones, dropping the pilot study and the press release from the section entirely.

Require the synthesis subagent to emit a confidence score for each statement, calibrated against the coordinator's historical accuracy, and to flag every statement scoring below the section's threshold.
Carry each source's own hedging and study design through into the report, and split the section so that findings the literature treats as settled sit apart from those still in dispute.

items.explanation: The defect is not missing provenance but missing strength of evidence. The pilot's authors characterized their own result as preliminary and described a nine-patient unblinded design; that characterization and that methodological context were dropped when the finding was flattened into a declarative sentence. The exam guide's requirement is that reports carry the original source's characterization and methodological context forward, and that they be structured with explicit sections separating well-established findings from contested or provisional ones, so a reader can weight each claim without going back to the corpus.

rationales.A: Claim-source mappings are a genuine requirement, but they are not what failed here: the reviewer could already see which document each statement came from. What was missing is what the source said about its own certainty, which an identifier and an excerpt of the finding do not convey.
rationales.B: Suppressing the two weaker sources hides the state of the evidence instead of reporting it. Publisher rank is not a measure of methodological strength, and a report that silently drops a preliminary result leaves the reader unable to see that the question is still open.
rationales.C: A score produced by the synthesizing model describes its own certainty about what it read, not the standing of the finding in its source. The pilot's caveats were stated in the paper and were available to carry forward; no self-assigned score reconstructs them, and calibrating against the coordinator's past accuracy measures a different thing again.

items.objective: 5.6 Preserve information provenance and handle uncertainty in multi-source synthesis

options.text: `search_result` blocks require the `search-results-2025-06-18` beta header; without it the blocks are accepted but passed to the model as ordinary text.

Citations are disabled by default for `search_result` blocks; each block needs `citations: {"enabled": true}`, and every search result in the request has to carry the same setting for it to take effect.
The `source` field must be a resolvable `https://` URL; an internal scheme such as `kb://` cannot be dereferenced, so the API discards the provenance metadata for that block.
`search_result` blocks are citable only when supplied as top-level content in a user message; returned inside a tool's `tool_result` they are treated as opaque tool output.

items.explanation: Unlike documents, search results have citations off by default. Each `search_result` block must set `citations: {"enabled": true}`, and the setting has to be consistent across all search results in the request. Adding it turns on the structured citation blocks that carry the source and title through to the consumer.

rationales.A: No beta header is required for `search_result` content blocks. Inventing a header requirement explains nothing about why the blocks were accepted and processed but produced no citations.
rationales.C: The `source` field accepts any stable string identifier, including internal schemes such as `kb://article-1234`. It is a provenance label, not a URL the API attempts to fetch.
rationales.D: Search results can be returned either from a custom tool's `tool_result` or supplied directly as top-level content in a user message. Both paths are supported and both are citable once citations are enabled.

items.objective: 5.6 Preserve information provenance and handle uncertainty in multi-source synthesis
items.stem: The coordinator of the research system is rewriting the output contract that every document-analysis subagent must satisfy before its findings are passed to synthesis. Reports have recently suffered from unattributable figures, from analysts silently choosing between disagreeing sources, and from a preliminary single-lab result being reported in the same register as a replicated industry survey. Which THREE requirements belong in that contract? (Select THREE)

options.text: Each subagent resolves disagreements internally by keeping the value from the higher-ranked publisher and dropping the other, so that the coordinator is handed exactly one number per metric.
Each subagent converts all of its findings, including financial tables and benchmark results, into one uniform bullet-list format before returning them to the coordinator.
Each subagent returns one self-reported score for the document as a whole, which the coordinator then uses in place of per-figure source attribution when it assembles the report.
Every extracted figure carries the source identifier it came from together with the verbatim excerpt that supports it, so the mapping survives into synthesis.
Every finding is labelled with how well established it is in its source, and the original source's own characterization and methodological caveats are carried through rather than dropped.
Conflicting figures from credible sources are both returned, each annotated with its own source attribution, and left for the coordinator to reconcile before synthesis.

items.explanation: The three defects map onto three contract requirements. Unattributable figures are fixed by per-figure source identifiers plus the supporting excerpt. A preliminary result reading like a settled one is fixed by carrying each source's own characterization and methodological caveats through, so the report can separate well-established findings from contested or provisional ones. Silent conflict resolution is fixed by returning both values with their attributions and reserving reconciliation for the coordinator, which is the layer that can see all the sources at once.

rationales.A: Letting each subagent pick a winner destroys exactly the signal the reader needs. Publisher rank is not a reconciliation rule, and dropping the losing value hides the disagreement from the coordinator, the only layer positioned to weigh all the sources together.
rationales.B: Flattening every finding to one format is the opposite of the required behaviour. Financial data belongs in tables, news in prose and technical findings in structured lists; uniform conversion makes figures harder to compare and drops table structure.
rationales.C: The granularity is wrong and it is offered as a substitute rather than an addition. One number for a whole filing cannot tell the coordinator which figure was drawn from which table, so replacing per-figure attribution with it reintroduces the unattributable figures the contract is meant to eliminate.

items.objective: 5.6 Preserve information provenance and handle uncertainty in multi-source synthesis
items.stem: A pipeline extracts sustainability metrics from supplier ESG reports into a JSON schema and feeds them to a reconciliation service. The service has raised 300 contradiction alerts where two Scope 1 emissions figures for the same supplier differ by more than the tolerance. Investigation shows that in nearly all cases the two figures are correct and come from different reporting years, because suppliers publish multiple annual reports. Which change removes the false contradictions without losing information?

options.text: Annotate each disagreeing pair as a conflict, attaching full source attribution to both values, and route the pair to a human reviewer who decides which of the two emissions figures is authoritative for that supplier.
Add a deduplication step that keeps only the most recently published figure for each supplier and metric and discards the older extraction before reconciliation runs.
Raise the extraction confidence threshold so that only high-confidence emissions figures reach the reconciliation service, cutting the volume of pairs that can disagree.
Require the extraction schema to carry the reporting period or data-collection date for every figure, so the reconciliation step reads the pair as a time series rather than a contradiction.

items.explanation: These are not conflicts, they are observations from different points in time that the schema gives the consumer no way to distinguish. Requiring publication or data-collection dates in the structured output lets the reconciliation step interpret two different values for the same supplier and metric correctly, and it is the specific fix for temporal differences being misread as contradictions.

rationales.A: Conflict annotation with source attribution is the right mechanism for a genuine disagreement between credible sources about the same period. Applied here it would send 300 correct, non-conflicting data points to reviewers who can only rediscover that the years differ.
rationales.B: Keeping only the newest value destroys the time series that the metric is most useful for, and the deduplication itself relies on knowing publication dates, which is the very metadata the schema is missing.
rationales.C: Confidence is unrelated to the problem. The figures are correctly extracted and would score high, so raising the threshold suppresses volume indiscriminately while leaving the temporal ambiguity in place.

items.objective: 5.6 Preserve information provenance and handle uncertainty in multi-source synthesis
items.stem: The synthesis agent in the research system currently flattens everything it receives into a single uniform bullet list: quarterly revenue figures from filings, market news from press coverage, and latency benchmark results from vendor documentation all come out as one-line bullets. Readers report that the quarterly figures are impossible to compare across periods and that the benchmark conditions have gone missing. Which instruction should the synthesis prompt carry?

options.text: Match the presentation to the shape of each finding: period-over-period figures in a grid the reader can scan down, narrative items as running text, and benchmark results as entries that keep their conditions attached.

Convert the whole report to markdown tables - financial data, news coverage and technical findings alike - so that the document is internally consistent from end to end and every value the reader might want to compare sits in a directly comparable cell.

Constrain the whole report with an `output_config.format` JSON schema, with `additionalProperties` set to false on every section object, so that each section is emitted in a fixed machine-checkable shape before it ever reaches the reader.
Shorten every bullet to a single sentence and drop qualifying detail, so that the reader can scan all three sections quickly and the report stays within a predictable length.

items.explanation: Different content types carry their meaning in different structures. A financial series needs a tabular layout to be comparable across periods, narrative news reads naturally as prose, and technical findings need a structured list that keeps conditions and caveats attached to each result. Forcing one uniform format destroys the structure that made each finding interpretable.

rationales.B: This substitutes one uniform format for another. Narrative market news and benchmark methodology notes do not decompose into table cells, so the readability problem simply moves to a different set of sections.
rationales.C: A rigid output schema enforces shape rather than suitability, and it would lock the report into exactly the uniformity being complained about. Report presentation is a synthesis instruction, not a schema constraint.
rationales.D: Truncating to one sentence per item removes the qualifying detail the readers are already missing, including the benchmark conditions, and does nothing to make the quarterly figures comparable.
